checked: spec/changes/ on 2026-11-12: 195 documents, 152 archived (145 change, 7 roadmap), 25 exploring, 8 approved change documents, 10 approved roadmaps, all in one flat folder
62e1482: the specs list gained a 'Not archived' phase filter that hides archived documents and archived roadmap slices; not the default
spec_lifecycle.py:672: documents carry superseded_at, which roadmap-done can read as folded
limits: Not yet read: every place that resolves a document by path (index, evidence, tasks, folds), which archive-folder must keep working; the file list in task 'archive-move' is a guess until then
Not yet read: how the specs list's current filter state is stored, so whether live-by-default replaces or reuses the 'Not archived' filter

open_questions.question: Should archiving still move files into spec/changes/archive/ (decided 2026-10-08), or is hiding archived documents in the list enough? Moving is the larger, riskier part: it rewrites paths the Hub, evidence and git history refer to.
What is the stall limit: 10 days for both flags (the 2026-11-08 assessment's line), or different limits for exploring and for approved-with-no-tasks?

Who sees the stalled flags: only the specs list, or also the tidy agent, so it can propose ending them? And should a done roadmap be archived automatically, or only shown as done for the operator to archive?

problem: On 2026-11-12, 152 of the 195 documents under spec/changes/ in this repository are archived (145 change documents, 7 roadmaps), all in one flat folder beside the 43 still in play. The specs list shows them together unless the operator picks the 'Not archived' phase filter added that morning (62e1482), so finding live work means reading past finished work. Roadmaps never end: 10 stay approved even when every slice is built. Documents also stall without anyone noticing: the 2026-11-08 assessment found 16 exploring for more than 10 days and 10 change documents approved that never got tasks. The archive subfolder decided on 2026-10-08 was never built.

requirements.rationale: Three quarters of this repository's documents are finished; the default view should serve the work in play.
requirements.statement: The specs list shows, by default, only documents that are not archived. It states how many finished documents it is hiding, and one action shows them, marked as finished. The choice is remembered per project.

requirements.rationale: Decided 2026-10-08 and never built: someone browsing the folder or the repository should see live work without the finished. Ids, not paths, are the durable identity, so the move must not break references.
requirements.statement: Archiving a document moves its files from spec/changes/<name>/ to spec/changes/archive/<name>/. Its id, requirement identifiers, history and every link to it by id keep working, and reading it by its old path still finds it.
Documents already archived when this ships are moved to the archive folder once, with the same guarantees as archive-folder.
A roadmap reads as done once every slice has a change document and every one of those is folded (superseded) or archived. The list and the roadmap's page show it as done.

A document is flagged as stalled when it has been exploring with no save for longer than the stall limit, or approved with no tasks and no build for longer than the stall limit. The flag says which, and since when.

in_scope: What the specs list shows by default, and a way to see finished documents
Where an archived document's files live
Flags for documents that have stalled
non_goals: Who may archive: archiving stays the operator's (the tidy agent marks superseded, the operator archives in a batch)
Changing requirement identity or the document lifecycle phases
Capability documents, which are current behaviour and never finish

summary: The specs list shows only documents still in play unless the operator asks for finished ones. A roadmap reads as done once every slice's change is folded or archived. Documents stuck in exploring too long, or approved with no tasks, are flagged so the operator or the tidy agent can end them.
